articles.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-5 with Native Multimodal Reasoning and Extended Context
articles.summary: OpenAI officially launched GPT-5 in late July 2026, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning across text, image, audio, and video inputs with a 1M token context window. The model demonstrates significant improvements in long-horizon planning and multi-step mathematical proofs, narrowing the gap with domain-specific expert systems in several benchmarks.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Scientific Discovery Benchmarks
articles.summary: DeepMind unveiled Gemini Ultra 2, which set new records on ScienceBench and MathOlympiad evaluation suites. The model introduces a novel architecture combining mixture-of-experts with retrieval-augmented generation at inference time, enabling it to synthesize findings across thousands of research papers in real time.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Deploys Humanoid Workers Across BMW's Spartanburg Plant
articles.summary: Figure AI announced a scaled deployment of its Figure 03 humanoid robots across BMW's South Carolina manufacturing facility, marking one of the largest commercial humanoid deployments to date. The robots handle parts kitting, quality inspection, and inter-station transport, reportedly improving line throughput by 14% during a six-month pilot.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Demonstrates Autonomous Warehouse Operations in Unstructured Environments
articles.summary: Tesla showcased its third-generation Optimus humanoid operating autonomously in a deliberately cluttered warehouse without pre-mapped environments. The robot leverages an on-device vision-language-action model fine-tuned on millions of hours of teleoperation data, enabling real-time object recognition, grasping, and adaptive path planning without cloud connectivity.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional Steering: Fine-Grained Runtime Safety Controls for Enterprise AI
articles.summary: Anthropic published a technical paper and product update detailing Constitutional Steering, a framework that allows enterprise customers to dynamically adjust safety and policy boundaries at inference time via structured constraint specifications. The approach decouples safety tuning from base model weights, enabling granular domain-specific deployment without retraining.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm GAA Process Node for Next-Gen AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed the start of volume production on its N1.4 process using gate-all-around transistor architecture at its Fab 20 facility in Tainan. The node delivers a 25% power efficiency improvement and 15% logic density gain over N2, with initial customers including NVIDIA and Apple targeting late-2026 and early-2027 product launches.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface with 4x Electrode Density
articles.summary: Neuralink obtained FDA clearance for its N2 implant, which quadruples the electrode count to over 4,000 channels while reducing surgical insertion time by 40%. Early clinical trial data from the first cohort of paralysis patients shows significantly improved cursor control bandwidth and the first demonstrations of reliable handwriting-speed text output via neural decoding.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Commercial Platform with Modular End-Effector System
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics launched the commercial version of its electric Atlas humanoid with a hot-swappable modular end-effector system supporting grippers, drills, and inspection sensors. The platform targets construction, oil and gas, and disaster response verticals, with Hyundai committing to a 500-unit initial deployment across its shipbuilding operations in Ulsan.
